harness: the bundle's own tests/manifest.json verifier_specs, unmodified, run through the vendored tests/rl_world_verifiers engine (the same code path benchmark_runner.py uses for file_check) against a workspace built from solution/artifact_plan.json
scope: the 7 core file_check verifiers. database_state, rubric_check and tool_execution verifiers are not workspace artifacts and are not mutable this way.

controls.positive: the oracle's own artifacts score every file_check
controls.semantic: one corrupted graded value fails EXACTLY the verifier that grades it
controls.granularity: one corrupted value fails exactly one verifier and the rest still pass, so reward drops by that entry's weight rather than to zero
controls.cosmetic: presentation changes that leave every number correct still score every file_check
controls.incompleteness: an artifact missing a graded value fails the verifier that grades it, rather than passing on a lenient lookup
controls.adversarial_acceptance: a plausible WRONG answer -- a superset report, or every figure off by one -- fails rather than scoring

residual_risk_duplicate_graded_key.note: a correct answer that also writes a breakdown reusing a graded key name. No clean fix: prompt clause is mitigation only, `contains` breaks the single-match case, `$..key[0]` fails every case. Not counted in brittleness.

cases.note: the batch-8 membership regex accepted a superset; an ordered column list must reject one. Reported but NOT counted in all_controls_pass, for the same reason the report-superset case is not: it measures the CHECK VOCABULARY, not the package. file_check has no set-equality or cardinality operator (see the connector report, verifier issue 3.1), and on a bundle whose figures are all scalars the appended row carries a NEW label (EXTRA-0), which the tolerance policy requires every label lookup to ignore - so this case cannot fail there by construction. Read superset_report_accepted for the finding itself.
